findings.title: Deep hierarchical page lacks breadcrumb navigation trail
findings.evidence: Observed at https://wordpress.org/news/2026/09/108-student-websites/ via breadcrumb_markup_inspector [2026-09-13T15:45:08Z]: Page at deep route (/news/2026/09/108-student-websites/) lacks breadcrumb UI or Schema.org BreadcrumbList markup for parent context. (Confidence: medium)

suggested_action.summary: Add breadcrumb navigation trail with BreadcrumbList schema.
suggested_action.how_to_fix: Add visual breadcrumb navigation and accompanying Schema.org BreadcrumbList JSON-LD to assist user orientation.
suggested_action.expected_benefit: Improves navigation by making the observed information clearer and more extractable for the intended audience.

evidence_details.observation: Page at deep route (/news/2026/09/108-student-websites/) lacks breadcrumb UI or Schema.org BreadcrumbList markup for parent context.

findings.severity_rationale: Rated low because the observed evidence indicates low impact; unavailable evidence is not treated as a defect.

evidence_ledger.observation: Page at deep route (/news/2026/09/108-student-websites/) lacks breadcrumb UI or Schema.org BreadcrumbList markup for parent context.

assessments.reason: robots.txt was fetched and its rules were applied to page and link fetches.
Initial HTML was inspected for shell signals; no browser rendering was used.
Answerability was checked against accessible on-site text and structured data only.
Only explicitly linked authority domains were inspected; external sources were not fabricated or searched.
No agent-supplied external discovery evidence was provided; no external search was performed.

proactive_recommendations.title: Mark up existing question-and-answer content with FAQPage schema
proactive_recommendations.rationale: The site already contains question-shaped content, but none of it is marked as FAQPage. FAQPage is the highest-leverage schema type for AI citation because its question/answer structure matches how retrieval systems chunk content and lift a quotable answer. The content already exists; only the markup is missing.

suggested_action.summary: Add FAQPage JSON-LD to pages that already answer common questions.
suggested_action.how_to_fix: Wrap each question and its answer in FAQPage JSON-LD with mainEntity -> Question -> acceptedAnswer. Mark up the answers you already publish rather than writing new ones.

proactive_recommendations.title: Add Article schema with author and dateModified to editorial pages
proactive_recommendations.rationale: 3 crawled page(s) are editorial or documentation content carrying no Article schema. Authorship and a machine-readable modification date are the signals assistants use to decide whether a passage is current and attributable -- without them, an assistant that finds a good answer on the page still has no basis to date it or credit it.

suggested_action.summary: Mark editorial and documentation pages with Article JSON-LD.
suggested_action.how_to_fix: Add Article or TechArticle JSON-LD with headline, author (a Person or Organization with a real profile URL), datePublished and dateModified. Update dateModified when the content genuinely changes, not on every deploy.

proactive_recommendations.title: Add BreadcrumbList schema to deep pages
proactive_recommendations.rationale: 1 crawled page(s) sit two or more levels deep with no BreadcrumbList markup. Breadcrumbs give both a visitor arriving cold from an AI answer and the assistant itself the parent context a deep URL otherwise lacks.

suggested_action.summary: Add BreadcrumbList JSON-LD alongside visible breadcrumb navigation.
suggested_action.how_to_fix: Emit BreadcrumbList JSON-LD listing each ancestor with position, name and item URL, and render the same trail visibly at the top of the page.

proactive_recommendations.title: State AI usage terms explicitly in robots.txt
proactive_recommendations.rationale: robots.txt names which agents may crawl but says nothing about what may be done with the content once fetched. Emerging conventions -- Cloudflare's Content Signals Policy (released CC0) and RSL licensing terms -- let a publisher separate training use from search indexing and answer generation in machine-readable form, instead of leaving that distinction to be inferred from which user agents happen to be listed.

suggested_action.summary: Add machine-readable content-usage signals to robots.txt.
suggested_action.how_to_fix: Add a Content Signals Policy block declaring your position on search, ai-input and ai-train separately, or publish RSL licensing terms. Keep it consistent with the agents you actually allow, or the two signals will contradict each other.

proactive_recommendations.title: Expose an agent-facing endpoint (NLWeb / MCP) built on existing structured data
proactive_recommendations.rationale: The site already publishes structured data, which is the input NLWeb uses to serve a conversational endpoint that AI agents can query directly rather than scraping HTML. Because it builds on schema.org markup, sitemaps and feeds you already maintain, it is incremental rather than a rebuild, and it moves the brand from being read by agents to being queryable by them.

suggested_action.summary: Evaluate an NLWeb instance exposing an /ask and /mcp endpoint over existing content.
suggested_action.how_to_fix: Point an NLWeb instance at your existing schema.org data and sitemap, and expose /ask and /mcp. Start with the content an agent is most likely to be asked about -- catalogue, docs, pricing.
